subject: Copywriting
title: The First Banner Ad
description: A short lesson to help you apply The First Banner Ad.

hook.text: In 1994, AT&T ran the first banner ad on HotWired. It said: 'Have you ever clicked your mouse right HERE?'

buildup.text: 44% of people who saw it clicked. Today's average click rate is 0.1%. Curiosity was powerful when ads were new.

discovery.text: Banner ads introduced measurability. For the first time, advertisers knew exactly how many people responded.

twist.text: Clickthrough rates collapsed as banners multiplied. 'Banner blindness' became the first digital ad problem.

climax.text: The banner ad split advertising in two: those who measure and those who guess. Digital chose measuring.

punchline.text: 44% clicked the first banner ad. Now 0.1% do. Novelty fades.

quiz.question: What was the click-through rate on the first banner ad?

details.summary: The first web banner ad appeared on HotWired.com on October 27, 1994, for AT&T. It read 'Have you ever clicked your mouse right HERE? You will' and achieved a 44% click-through rate — a number that has declined to about 0.05% today. This single ad launched the digital advertising industry.
details.whyItMatters: The first banner ad marks the beginning of digital advertising. Its 44% CTR compared to today's 0.05% illustrates how novelty drives initial engagement and how audiences develop ad blindness over time.
takeaways: The first banner ad appeared on HotWired.com in October 1994
It achieved a 44% click-through rate — versus about 0.05% today
Banner ads launched the multi-billion-dollar digital ad industry

faq.question: Why was the first banner ad's click rate so high?
faq.answer: Novelty. Nobody had seen a clickable ad before. The curious, interactive nature of 'click here' was irresistible to early web users. As banner ads proliferated, users developed 'banner blindness' — the ability to unconsciously ignore rectangular ads on web pages.

faq.question: How did banner ads change advertising?
faq.answer: They created a new advertising medium with unprecedented measurability. For the first time, advertisers could track exactly how many people saw, clicked, and acted on an ad. This data-driven approach eventually displaced the gut-instinct methods of traditional advertising.
